sections.title: Is the price fair?
sections.intro: Asking price per m² against similar flats for sale now. Contract prices are usually a few % lower than asking.

items.head: ¥533k/m² — the cheapest of 15 comparable flats
items.detail: Comparable = 90 m²+ used condos for sale now in Chiba Mihama, built 2005–2015.
items.cmp: Median ¥609k/m² · range ¥533k–757k · all ages in the area: median ¥623k/m² (54 flats)

items.head: Much cheaper than its peers — find out why
items.detail: Typical reasons: low floor, poor orientation, a view blocked by a newer building, an upcoming levy, a structural or legal issue, a stigma (告知事項), or a seller in a hurry.
items.ask: Why is it priced below similar flats? How long has it been on the market and has the price changed?

sections.title: What it really costs
sections.intro: Monthly running costs, how the fees compare, and the one-off costs of buying.

items.head: Repair fund ¥15,100/month = ¥165/m²
items.detail: MLIT guideline for a building like this (under 20 floors, 5,000–10,000 m², floor area estimated ~5,700 m²): average ¥252/m², ⅔ of buildings ¥170–320. (The floor area is a rough estimate near the 5,000 m² line — the smaller band's average is ¥335/m².) At the guideline average this flat would pay ≈ ¥23,073/month (+¥7,973). A fund below the guideline usually means future increases or a one-off levy (一時金).
items.cmp: Peers built ±5 years (428 watchlist condos): median ¥196/m², middle half ¥140–240 → this flat is at the 38th percentile.
items.ask: Please share the 長期修繕計画 and the current repair-fund balance. Are increases or a 一時金 planned?

items.head: Management fee ¥16,200/month = ¥177/m² (委託(通勤))
items.detail: Small buildings cost more per flat; staffed (常駐) management costs more than visiting (巡回).
items.cmp: Peers of similar age and size (0–60 units): median ¥177/m² → 50th percentile (70 condos)

items.head: Other fixed monthly charges ¥1,680
items.detail: インターネット定額料金 ¥1,260 · CATV定額料金 ¥420

items.head: ≈ ¥170,735/month before parking and property tax

items.ask: What was the last 固定資産税・都市計画税 bill for this unit?

items.head: One-off buying costs ≈ ¥3,140,400–¥4,116,400
items.detail: Agent fee (仲介手数料, 3% + ¥60k + tax) ¥1,676,400 · plus registration tax and scrivener, loan fees and guarantee, fire + earthquake insurance, stamp duty, pro-rated property tax and fees: typically 3–5% of the price.

sections.title: Earthquake safety

items.head: Built 2010-10 — current seismic standard (新耐震)
items.detail: The rule depends on the building-permit date (from June 1981); completion from spring 1983 is almost always new-standard.

items.head: Structure: RC, 5 floors
items.detail: RC/SRC are the norm for condos.

items.head: 30-year chance of shaking ≥ 6-lower here: 73% (≥ 6-upper: 23%)
items.detail: ≥ 5-upper: 99%. Modern buildings are designed for this; the risk is contents, lifts, pipes and the days without water or power.
items.cmp: Study areas (population-weighted, ≥ 6-lower): median 59%, range 24–89% → rank 62 of 78 from the safest

items.head: Ground: 埋立地 — shaking amplified ×1.80
items.detail: Soft ground amplifies shaking (AVS30 201 m/s; about 1.6 or more counts as soft). Ask how the building is founded (piles to bearing stratum?).
items.ask: What kind of foundation does the building have (支持層までの杭基礎)?

sections.title: Water and ground
sections.intro: Depth bands are the maximum assumed scenario (想定最大規模) at SUUMO's map point; SUUMO's point is approximate, so the worst value within ~100 m is shown too.

items.head: River flood: 0.5–3 m at the point
items.detail: The flat is on floor 3: it stays dry, but entrances, parking, lifts and the building's electrical room may not. Expect days without lifts/water if the electrical room floods.
items.ask: Where are the electrical room (電気室), water pumps and parking — basement or ground floor? Any flood barriers (止水板)?

items.head: Storm surge: 0.5–3 m at the point
items.detail: The flat is on floor 3: it stays dry, but entrances, parking, lifts and the building's electrical room may not. Expect days without lifts/water if the electrical room floods.
items.ask: Where are the electrical room (電気室), water pumps and parking — basement or ground floor? Any flood barriers (止水板)?

items.head: Liquefaction tendency: high
items.detail: Landform: 盛土地･埋立地 on 旧水部 (国土地理院). Condo towers on piles usually stand, but roads, pipes, gas and sewers around them can fail for weeks (as in Urayasu 2011).
items.ask: Was the building or site damaged in 2011 (東日本大震災)? Ground improvement?

items.head: Area context (Chiba Mihama)
items.cmp: 95% of residents live in some water zone · 97% on high-liquefaction ground · 0.5% in landslide zones

items.head: Old maps
items.detail: Check what the site was before (sea, paddy, river) on 今昔マップ; past disaster records and 大規模盛土 maps come with the MLIT API key.

items.head: 2 different line(s) listed
items.detail: A second line is a fallback when one line stops (Keiyo line is often stopped by wind).

items.head: Management: 委託(通勤)
items.detail: 常駐 = resident manager, 日勤/通勤 = manager on weekdays.

items.head: 50 units
items.detail: Enough owners to share fixed costs.

items.head: Age 16 years — 1st major repair (外壁・屋上防水) due around now
items.detail: Major repairs come every ~12–15 years. Ask whether the last one was done on time and paid from the fund (not by a levy or loan).
items.ask: When was the last 大規模修繕, what did it cover and how was it paid? What is planned next?

items.head: Key documents decide this section
items.detail: 重要事項調査報告書 (fund balance, arrears, loans of the association), 総会議事録 (last 2–3 years), 長期修繕計画, 管理規約・使用細則.
items.ask: Can I see the 重要事項調査報告書 and the last 2–3 years of 総会議事録?

items.head: Floor 3 of 5
items.detail: Middle floor: neighbours above and below insulate.

items.head: Corner unit (角住戸)
items.detail: More windows and light; slightly more heat loss.

items.head: 91.56 m² (壁芯) ≈ 86.1 m² registered
items.detail: The tax rules (mortgage credit ≥ 50 m²) use the registered 内法 area, about 5–8% smaller than the advertised 壁芯 area.

sections.title: Energy, windows and running cost
sections.intro: Energy labels are only required for new buildings (from April 2024): used flats almost never show them, so proxies are used.

items.head: No energy label (normal for used flats)
items.ask: Is there a 住宅性能評価書, BELS or 長期優良住宅 certificate?

items.head: Likely designed to 1999 rules (次世代省エネ, ~today's 等級4)
items.detail: Era is only a hint: condos were not required to meet the energy standard until 2025.

items.head: Window type not stated
items.detail: In condos the window frames are common property: you usually cannot replace them yourself; inner windows (内窓) are allowed and subsidised.
items.ask: Are the windows single or double glazed? Were sashes replaced in a major repair?

items.head: Gas type not stated
items.detail: Propane (LPG) costs much more than city gas.
items.ask: City gas or propane? Electricity contract (high-voltage bulk 一括受電)?

items.head: Mortgage tax credit: eligible
items.detail: Built 1982 or later ✓ · registered area ≥ 50 m² ✓. Without an energy certificate a used home falls in the basic tier: 0.7% of the loan balance up to ¥20M for 10 years (max ¥140k/year). With a 省エネ基準適合 certificate it is 13 years; ZEH-level / 長期優良 raises the cap to ¥35M.
